title: Install and operate Mentor email practice
summary: Initialize or configure paused Mentor state, install its program/provider release, operate the exact worker binding, and use owned maintenance for drained updates and metadata backups.
use_when: Install, initialize, configure, inspect, pause, schedule, hold, drain, update or recover the Mentor mail service.
do_not_use_when: The task is desktop Mentor operation, direct database repair, provider credential or DNS changes, or an unapproved live practice run.
outcome: The selected Mentor program, state and worker binding have explicit product-owned configuration and maintenance boundaries without importing desktop state or creating an implicit live schedule.

interfaces.label: Select receiving route and Email wrapper
Inspect local compatibility and executable presence

effects: Initialization creates private schema-one state with the bundled corpus and paused configuration. Configure/import/pause/resume modify only Mentor-owned records.
Explicit schedule enable registers and selects the exact installed worker; disable affects only mentor/worker. Installation selects product/provider artifacts without enabling practice.
Maintenance owns one hold; a drain pass can finish already admitted grading and send work and perform expiry. Migration copies only drained metadata/corpus state to a private backup.
authority: Mentor owns its private state, admission, configuration, corpus import and exact worker definition. Clockwork owns binding mechanics and LaunchAgent/runtime records.
Cell coordinated deployment owns initialized release updates and recovery ordering. Email and Nucleus keep credential and execution authority.
success: Initialization returns paused supported state without scheduling. Configuration/import commits selected values while preserving existing assignments.

A successful schedule operation returns the supported selected binding state; it is separate from Mentor pause and practice success. A supported backup follows drain with no pending text or unresolved jobs/cancellation.
failure_and_recovery: Reject unsupported state or unsafe paths without creating a second database. Preserve owned holds when drain, backup, dependency readiness or rollback cannot be established.

Direct first installation is limited to uninitialized state. Disable mentor/worker before initialized coordinated deployment, then explicitly enable the desired current release afterward. Direct selector recovery is unsupported.
privacy: State is separate from desktop Mentor under Application Support/MentorMail. Neither configuration nor Clockwork definitions contain provider credentials, answers or critiques.
Migration refuses pending content and unresolved work before copying. Product backups do not erase Nucleus, Resend or inbox records.
does_not_authorize: Sending new practice mail merely because installation or initialization was requested, enabling an unrequested schedule, overriding another owner hold, publishing a release, or changing Email/Nucleus credentials.
steps: Read Mentor practice and installation contracts and affected installed provider contracts.
Use the product initialization/configuration commands; keep program installation, pause/resume and schedule enable separate.
For initialized updates, disable the exact worker, use maintained Cell deployment, drain existing work and require a content-free private backup.
Inspect the resulting program, state and binding under the operation authority; resume or enable only the intended admission/binding.
checkpoints: State root remains MentorMail, not the desktop Mentor state.
The worker has one exact immutable release, HOME only, interval 60, no run-at-load, overlap skip and timeout 90.
No unresolved pending content or cancellation is copied into migration backups.
Provider receipts, Nucleus observations and Clockwork runtime records remain separate success evidence.
adaptation: If a provider capability is absent, complete its separately authorized compatible installation before enabling dependent work.
Preserve other owner holds and existing admission pauses across coordinated updates.
stop_when: An initialized state update attempts direct selector recovery or occurs with an enabled worker.
Private-state, ownership, drain, dependency capability or backup requirements cannot be established.

consumers.statement: The current-user operator uses Mentor-owned administration and the maintained Cell installation path for initialized updates.

preconditions.statement: Administrative authority is separate from practice execution. A first install requires uninitialized state; initialized update/recovery requires coordinated maintenance and a disabled Mentor worker. Scheduling requires the canonical root and a selected immutable installed release.

inputs.statement: Administrative inputs are validated daily time, IANA zone, optional first delivery date in exact YYYY-MM-DD form interpreted in that zone, lowercase DNS receiving domain whose complete assignment mailbox fits 254 bytes, absolute Email wrapper path, schema-one corpus file, owner token and private absolute backup destination. A pre-existing backup must exactly match drained state and is not overwritten.

outputs.statement: Commands return ok:true with selected operation data under data when --json is requested. Maintenance observations use protocol_version 1 inside data.maintenance. Failure returns ok:false with an error detail. Status counts cover retained records, not lifetime totals; no pending content is exposed. First migration initializes paused schema-one state and returns backup:null.

data_semantics.statement: Paused admission, an enabled Clockwork binding, a maintained hold, a drained queue, a selected release and accepted practice mail are independent states. Initialization does not enable scheduling; enabling a schedule does not clear pause.

identity_and_units.statement: Canonical application root is MentorMail; product/provider identity is mentor; stable schedule key is mentor/worker. Release definitions pin immutable executable identity. Daily time is a local HH:MM in an IANA zone; runtime metadata timestamps use Unix seconds UTC.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Doctor inspects only local installation/state compatibility and Email executable presence. Email API/receiving permission, Nucleus execution readiness and live delivery are explicitly not_probed. Schedule status reads the supported owned binding. Drain performs one bounded recovery pass and may require repetition.
No future activation, deadline during downtime, provider mail retention or final inbox delivery is established by administration reads.

access.statement: Private current-user files and an exclusive product runner protect state. Configure and installed schedule operations reject unsupported paths or foreign definitions. Email and Nucleus credentials remain provider-owned.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Initialization is separate from install. Schedule enable selects current exact release and leaves admission pause unchanged. Initialized deployment requires the supported maintained coordinator and disabled worker; direct recovery is rejected. Backup requires drained work and no pending text. Holds persist until the same owner releases them.

operational_limits.statement: The product supports one canonical scheduled state root, one worker binding, schema-one state, and no desktop database import. Timer delivery, provider operations and state rollback retain their independent limits.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Unsupported database versions fail. There is no predecessor state format or incompatible binary-only rollback. Program and Chancery bundle are staged together; enabling the worker pins the selected release.
No general cross-release compatibility window or deployment duration is promised.

reliances.statement: Email owns fixed-recipient submission, exact reply metadata and accepted provider receipts. Mentor uses its installed-wrapper typed client; it does not load the credential.
Email owns bounded account receiving reads and their metadata/content semantics. Mentor owns account-read authority, routing and duplicate handling.
Nucleus owns exact constrained job execution, capability readiness, job identity, cancellation and retained execution records.
Clockwork owns exact registered worker activation and runtime observations, not daily selection or practice completion.
Initialized installation and recovery use Cell maintained deployment and shared content-addressed file transactions.
